title: BACE: Equipment & Experimental Design - BACE - Standard Equipment
subject: BACE

questions.q: When operating a centrifuge, which of the following practices is **critical** to prevent damage to the drive shaft and potential injury?
options: Setting the timer to at least 10 minutes
Ensuring the rotor is balanced by placing tubes of equal mass opposite each other
Using glass tubes for speeds above 20,000 RPM
Setting the temperature to 4°C for all spin cycles
questions.explain: Centrifuges must be balanced to distribute the load evenly around the rotor. An unbalanced rotor can cause the centrifuge to wobble, damaging the drive shaft and potentially causing catastrophic failure. Source: Eppendorf Centrifugation Basics.
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: A technician needs to autoclave 500 mL of liquid media. Which autoclave cycle parameters are appropriate to prevent the liquid from boiling over during the exhaust phase?
options: Flash cycle with zero exhaust time
questions.explain: The 'Liquid' cycle uses a slow exhaust (or gravity displacement with slow vent) to allow the pressure to decrease gradually. A fast exhaust would cause the superheated liquid to boil over violently due to the rapid drop in pressure.
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: Calculate the Relative Centrifugal Force (RCF) or 'g-force' if the rotor radius ($r​$) is 10 cm and the speed is 3000 RPM. Use the approximation formula: $$RCF = 1.12 \times 10^{-5} \times r \times (RPM)^2$$
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: You need to pipette 15 $\mu$L of a reagent. Which pipette would provide the highest accuracy and precision?
questions.explain: Pipettes are most accurate in the upper range of their capacity. A P20 (2-20 $\mu$L) is ideal for 15 $\mu$L. A P200 is less accurate at its lower limit, and a P10 cannot hold 15 $\mu$L.
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: When using a light microscope with an oil immersion objective (100x), why is immersion oil required?
options: To lubricate the slide and prevent scratching the lens
To match the refractive index of glass, preventing light scattering and increasing resolution
To cool the objective lens during high-intensity illumination
To stain the specimen for better contrast
questions.explain: Immersion oil has a refractive index (~1.51) similar to glass. It bridges the gap between the slide and the lens, preventing light refraction (bending) that would occur in air, thus increasing the Numerical Aperture and resolution.
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: What is the standard temperature and pressure typically used in an autoclave for sterilization?
questions.explain: Standard autoclaving parameters are 121°C (250°F) at 15 psi (pounds per square inch) for 15-20 minutes.
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: If a spectrophotometer reads an Absorbance ($A​$) of 1.0, what percentage of light is transmitted through the sample? (Formula: $A = -\log_{10} T$)
questions.explain: Use the formula: $$1.0 = -\log_{10} T$$ ​$$\log_{10} T = -1$$ ​$$T = 10^{-1} = 0.1$$ Converting to percentage: $0.1 \times 100\% = 10\%$.
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: When balancing a centrifuge with an odd number of tubes (e.g., 3 tubes) in a 12-slot fixed-angle rotor, how should they be arranged?
options: Place them side-by-side in slots 1, 2, and 3
Place them in slots 1, 5, and 9 to form an equilateral triangle
It is impossible to balance 3 tubes; a dummy tube must be added
Place two opposite each other and one in the center
questions.explain: Three tubes can be balanced in a 12-slot rotor by spacing them equally apart (forming an equilateral triangle). Slots 1, 5, and 9 are equidistant (4 slots apart).
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: Identify the primary function of a **Laminar Flow Hood** in a tissue culture lab.
options: To protect the user from hazardous chemical fumes
To provide a sterile environment for the sample using HEPA-filtered air
questions.explain: Laminar Flow Hoods blow HEPA-filtered sterile air over the workspace to protect the *sample* from contamination. They do not typically protect the user (unlike Biosafety Cabinets).
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: A swinging-bucket rotor is preferred over a fixed-angle rotor for which application?
options: Pelleting nucleic acids at very high speeds
Separating samples in density gradients (e.g., Ficoll)
questions.explain: Swinging-bucket rotors allow tubes to swing out to a horizontal position. This is ideal for density gradient centrifugation because the gradient layers remain horizontal and are not disturbed when the rotor stops.
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: Before weighing a chemical on an analytical balance, the user presses the 'Tare' button. What does this do?
options: Calibrates the balance using an internal weight
Resets the display to zero, subtracting the weight of the weigh boat
Turns off the draft shield static
Converts the units from grams to milligrams
questions.explain: Taring re-zeros the balance. It accounts for the container (weigh boat) so that only the mass of the added substance is displayed.
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: Which biological indicator is commonly used to validate the efficacy of an autoclave cycle?
questions.explain: *Geobacillus stearothermophilus* spores are highly heat-resistant. If the autoclave kills these spores, it is assumed to have killed all other common pathogens.
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: Microscope maintenance: What is the proper material to clean objective lenses?
questions.explain: Lens paper is specifically designed to be soft and non-abrasive. Paper towels and Kimwipes are too rough and can scratch the optical coating. Acetone can dissolve lens cement.
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: Which part of the spectrophotometer separates the white light into its component wavelengths?
questions.explain: The monochromator (diffraction grating or prism) disperses light into specific wavelengths and selects a narrow band to pass through the sample.
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: What is the primary risk of using a pipette tip that does not fit tightly?
options: Air leakage will prevent accurate volume aspiration
questions.explain: Air displacement pipettes rely on an airtight seal. If the tip is loose, air leaks in during aspiration, resulting in less liquid being drawn up than the set volume.
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: In the context of equipment calibration, what does 'NIST-traceable' mean?
options: The equipment was manufactured by NIST
The calibration standards used can be traced back to the National Institute of Standards and Technology reference standards
questions.explain: NIST-traceability ensures an unbroken chain of comparisons to national standards, guaranteeing the accuracy of the measurements.
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: When troubleshooting a pH meter that gives unstable readings, which is the most likely cause?
options: The electrode junction is clogged or dried out
The sample is at room temperature
The beaker is made of glass
questions.explain: pH electrodes require a hydrated junction to allow ion flow. A clogged or dry junction disrupts this flow, causing drifting or unstable readings.
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: Which class of Biosafety Cabinet (BSC) protects the worker, the environment, and the product (sample)?
questions.explain: Class II BSCs use HEPA filtered air to protect the sample (downflow air), and inward airflow to protect the user, with filtered exhaust to protect the environment. Class I protects only the user/environment. Clean benches protect only the sample.
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: When autoclaving waste bags, why must the bag be loosely tied or left slightly open?
options: To allow steam to penetrate the inside of the bag
To prevent the bag from melting
To let the bad smell escape
To allow easy addition of more waste later
questions.explain: Steam sterilization requires direct contact between steam and the material. If the bag is sealed tight, air is trapped inside, preventing steam penetration and resulting in incomplete sterilization.
questions.subject: BACE

questions.q: What is the function of the condenser on a light microscope?
options: To focus light onto the specimen
To capture the image for a camera
To move the stage up and down
questions.explain: The condenser is located below the stage and concentrates/focuses the light from the illuminator onto the specimen.
